en.title: Elden Ring's Messmer May Become the Next James Bond
en.summary: The actor behind Elden Ring's terrifying Messmer the Impaler is reportedly a frontrunner to don the iconic tuxedo. Denis Villeneuve is reportedly eyeing the star for the next 007 installment.
en.body:
The Lands Between might be losing one of its most formidable figures, not to the Tarnished, but to the world of espionage. **Jack Barton**, the actor who brought the menacing **Messmer the Impaler** to life in **Elden Ring**'s highly anticipated *Shadow of the Erdtree* expansion, is reportedly in contention to become the next **James Bond**.

This potential casting news comes from PageSix, which suggests that director **Denis Villeneuve** and casting director **Nina Gold** are exploring a range of fresh faces for the iconic role. Barton, whose sole video game credit is his impactful performance as Messmer, is said to be among a slate of contenders who will undergo screen tests in early September. While Barton's video game experience is limited, his presence in the critically acclaimed **Elden Ring** expansion showcases his ability to embody a powerful and memorable character. His resume also includes appearances in television series like **SAS: Rogue Heroes** and **War of the Worlds**, as well as a role in **Yorgos Lanthimos**'s Oscar-winning film **Poor Things**.

## A New 007 Era Dawns

The search for the next **James Bond** has been ongoing since **Daniel Craig**'s departure in *No Time to Die* in 2021. **Amazon MGM Studios**, having acquired the franchise, is reportedly keen on ushering in a new era for the spy saga. Director **Denis Villeneuve**, known for his work on the **Dune** films and **Blade Runner 2049**, is tasked with steering the franchise forward. The selection process is said to be focusing on "a stream of unknowns," a strategy that has yielded success for the Bond franchise in the past, notably with **Sean Connery** and **Daniel Craig** themselves. Other actors reportedly in the mix for screen tests include **Jack Lowden**, **Callum Turner**, **Jacob Elordi**, **Paul Mescal**, and **Harris Dickson**.

## Fan Reactions and Franchise Futures

For **Elden Ring** fans, the prospect of **Jack Barton** stepping into **James Bond**'s shoes is a fascinating crossover. Messmer the Impaler was a central antagonist in the *Shadow of the Erdtree* DLC, a character defined by his imposing presence and a mysterious, dark backstory. Barton's portrayal lent him an air of gravitas and menace that has clearly caught the attention of the Bond casting team. This move, if it materializes, would mark a significant career leap for Barton and underscore the growing influence of video game performances in broader entertainment. The gaming community often celebrates when actors from their favorite titles achieve mainstream success, and this rumor has certainly ignited discussion online about Barton's potential on the global stage.

## What's Next

Screen tests for the role of **James Bond** are expected to begin in early September. Further details regarding **Denis Villeneuve**'s vision for the next installment and official casting announcements are anticipated in the coming months as **Amazon MGM Studios** continues its deliberate search for the next cinematic icon.

content_raw: Following the report that said Battlefield 1's Jack Lowden is circling the role of James Bond for the next 007 movie, it’s now rumored that another actor who appeared in a video game, Jack Barton, could be in the mix as well. PageSix reported that Bond 26 director Denis Villeneuve and casting director Nina Gold are looking at a "stream of unknowns" to play James Bond next. One such person is Barton, who played Messmer the Impaler in Elden Ring's Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. That is Barton's only video game credit. On TV, he appeared in Steven Knight's SAS: Rogue Heroes and the TV show War of the Worlds. In film, Barton appeared in Yorgos Lanthimos' Oscar-winning 2023 movie Poor Things. The report went on to say Barton will do a screen test to play James Bond, as will other contenders, including Lowden. These tests will begin in early September and will also reportedly include people like Callum Turner, Jacob Elordi, Paul Mescal, and Harris Dickson. In May this year, Bond movie production company Amazon MGM Studios said the search for the next James Bond actor was underway and that the film studio would not comment on the casting process. It has been a long wait for the next James Bond movie, as the latest entry, No Time to Die, was released in 2021. However, it was expected to be release much sooner, but had three delays due in part to COVID. Daniel Craig played James Bond in five 007 films, and wrapped up his run with No Time To Die. Amazon MGM Studios bought the franchise and reportedly paid a lot of money to regain creative control from the longtime series stewards Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson. The new James Bond movie will be directed by Villeneuve, the Oscar-nominated filmmaker known for the Dune franchise. He’s also directed the movies Prisoners, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival.
